analysis.title: The Global Week Ahead (October 30, 2026): Checks and Balances
key_insights: US midterms on Tuesday: Scotiabank cites polls and betting markets showing high odds of a Democratic sweep of both the House and Senate. Full results may take days or weeks if races are close or contested.

The author expects escalation of US strikes against Iran shortly after the midterm vote. Trade policy, geopolitical risk, fiscal policy and AI regulation are named as areas the election result could affect.

October nonfarm payrolls (Friday): Scotia forecasts +100k vs consensus +60k and a prior +29k, with unemployment steady at 4.2%. The call rests on health-sector hiring pulled forward by an early flu season, plus mild October weather helping construction, leisure and hospitality.

Flu cases are tracking about four weeks ahead of recent years, with parts of the US at January levels. In 2022-23, October added over 110k health jobs not seasonally adjusted, or 63k seasonally adjusted. The author says the seasonal adjustment effect is uncertain.
The author warns that sickness- and weather-driven payroll strength may not reflect underlying labour market health and could mean hiring is pulled forward from later months.

Large layoff announcements may lift Challenger job cuts on Thursday: 60,000 buyouts at Microsoft, 5,000 at Barclays and 3,500 at Amex. The author says these are likely to affect payrolls in coming months.
Payroll revisions may be large because the September survey response rate was low. Scotia estimates Q3 US productivity at about 2.5% q/q SAAR, which should keep unit labour cost growth mild.

Canadian jobs (Friday): Scotia forecasts +15k vs consensus +18k, with unemployment at 6.5%. This follows losses of 68k in September and 42k in August. A third straight fall outside a recession or major shock would be highly unusual, and the author discounts September's loss as a labour-force and survey distortion.

Bank of Canada Governor Macklem and Senior Deputy Governor Rogers testify to the House Finance Committee and the Senate banking committee. The author expects Macklem to downplay recent GDP disappointments.

RBA expected to hike 25bp to 4.85% on Monday night ET, the fifth hike and 125bp of tightening this year. OIS prices 20bp. CPI has surprised to the upside and Governor Bullock has warned of inflation upside risks.

Banco Central do Brasil (Wednesday): Selic expected on hold at 13.75%, with a minority expecting a cut. Markets removed easing pricing after Lula's election win. The real fell about 9% vs the dollar in the past week and the 2-year yield is up about 115bp since August.
Banxico expected to hold at 6.5% on Thursday. September CPI was about 3.5% y/y with core at 3.8%, and the peso has weakened over 10% since September.

Riksbank (Wednesday): consensus is unanimous for a hike to 2.0%, which would be its first since 2023. Markets price 70% odds in the text and 17bp in the Central Bank Watch note, so the report's own figures differ.
Norges Bank expected to hold the deposit rate at 4.5% after hikes in May and September. The bank has signalled a longer hold, with a hawkish bias.

Bank of England expected to hike 25bp to 4.00% on Thursday. It is fully priced and consensus is unanimous. The author says the BoE is under pressure from energy costs feeding into broader prices, and updated forecasts matter.
Bank Negara Malaysia expected to hold at 2.75%. Fuel subsidies keep reported inflation at 1.8% y/y.

Canada's Budget 2026 on November 5 is expected to be expansionary. The Productivity Mega Deduction is costed at $36bn over five years. Scotia estimates $60bn of new spending announced since April and a final package near $80bn would not surprise. Deficits would still narrow toward the mid-to-high 1% of GDP range.

Euro area flash October CPI on Wednesday is one of the last two readings before the ECB's December meeting. Markets price about 20bp of tightening. New Zealand's labour report on Tuesday matters given an 85% market chance of a 25bp December RBNZ hike.

sector_views.rationale: Early flu season is expected to front-load health sector hiring into the October payrolls report.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Scotia is above consensus on early flu-season health hiring and mild weather, and warns the strength may be pulled forward from later months.
Scotia expects a modest rebound and discounts September's drop as a survey distortion.
Followed -42k in August. Scotia attributes much of it to labour force exits, youth job losses and survey quirks.

macro_indicators.reading: about 2.5% q/q SAAR (Scotia estimate); consensus 2.7%; prior 1.4%
macro_indicators.interpretation: Solid productivity would hold unit labour cost growth to a mild rise.
Fifth hike this year, 125bp cumulative, with OIS pricing 20bp.
Fully priced. Likely the start of a gradual tightening cycle.
First hike since 2023. Market odds differ between the report's text and its Central Bank Watch note.
A minority expects a cut. Markets removed easing after the election and the real's drop.
Higher inflation and a weaker peso reduce the urgency to cut.
Bias remains hawkish but the bank has signalled a longer hold.
Inflation is low at 1.8% y/y because of fuel subsidies.
Gauges whether price pressures are broadening ahead of the ECB's December meeting.

risk_factors: Midterm results may be contested or slow to count, leaving control of Congress unclear.
Payroll strength from flu and weather may reverse later, and low September survey response raises revision risk.
Large layoff announcements at Microsoft, Barclays and Amex may weigh on future payrolls.
Energy-price pass-through to broader inflation raises second-round risks for the BoE and RBA.
Brazilian fiscal easing combined with a weaker real could add to inflation pressure.
The Canadian budget adds spending and could strain skilled labour and add inflation before capacity expands.
vol_and_positioning: Markets price about 20bp of ECB tightening by December and an 85% chance of a 25bp RBNZ December hike.
The BoE hike is fully priced, the RBA hike is 20bp priced in OIS, and the Riksbank hike is priced at 70% in the text, or 17bp in the Central Bank Watch note.
geopolitical: US strikes against Iran may escalate soon after the US midterm vote
US midterm elections could change trade policy and fiscal policy and affect AI regulation
New US tariffs on three-wheeled Canadian vehicles, which the author does not consider a major shock
Brazil's election returned Lula, followed by capital flight and a weaker real
Middle East developments and elevated energy prices feed inflation risk for the RBA and BoE

tension_points.bull_case: Scotia expects +100k vs 60k consensus. Early flu season lifts health hiring, mild weather helps outdoor sectors, and job postings and seasonal openings are up.
tension_points.bear_case: Strength from illness and weather may say little about true labour market health and could be pulled forward from later months. Large layoffs and noisy revisions add risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A weaker unadjusted payroll gain or a seasonal adjustment factor different from last year's would undercut the forecast.

tension_points.bull_case: Two-month job losses of 100k or more rarely become a third straight drop outside a recession, and September was distorted by labour force exits, youth jobs and survey quirks.
tension_points.bear_case: Falling small business hiring plans conflict with rising job postings, and a third decline would signal real weakness.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A third consecutive monthly decline in October employment would challenge the rebound view.

theme_stances.key_argument: Early flu season and mild weather should boost health and outdoor-sector hiring.
